source_text: Cur putes, inquit, sine consecrationibus legis ad Abrahae stemma nationes non posse perduci, cum constet promissionem, quae facta est ad Abraham, anteriorem fuisse quam legem nec eam ablutionibus tributam fuisse, sed moribus?
pass_a_gloss: Why do you think, he says, that without the consecrations of the law nations cannot be led through to Abraham's stem, when it stands that the promise which was made to Abraham was earlier than the law and that it was not attributed to washings, but to manners?

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Why, he asks, do you think the nations cannot be brought into Abraham’s family without the law’s consecrations, when it is established that the promise made to Abraham preceded the law and was granted not for washings but for conduct (compare Romans 4:13–15)?

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
